title: Awwwards UI
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: text-safe README project cover for an open-source creative frontend skill
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity wide editorial project-cover composition presenting a creative operating system through five distinct visual worlds. This must be a purely visual cover with absolutely no typography anywhere.
Scene/backdrop: An ink-black presentation field with luminous bone panels, restrained signal-red accents, precise crop marks, unlabeled grid ticks, and layered browser-frame fragments. The frames open into five clearly different portals: a monochrome editorial fashion portrait, radial fluorescent microscopy and biotech specimen imagery, public-market evidence expressed only as blank newsprint rows with hard rules and one unlabeled graph trace, tactile cobalt/apricot collectible objects, and a cinematic alpine observatory. The portals must read as distinct worlds while the cover remains one coherent system.
Style/medium: premium art-direction deck, photographed materiality plus crisp interface composition, restrained Swiss editorial rigor with experimental Awwwards-level tension, implementation-clear desktop UI reference.
Composition/framing: 16:9 landscape. Keep the entire left third visually quiet with generous negative space, subtle grid structure, and one narrow vertical bone rail only, so an editable README heading below the image can carry the project name. Build a strong left-to-right reading path as the five asymmetric portal frames grow across the center and right. Use controlled overlaps, sharp rectangular geometry, exact gutters, and deep breathing room. No centered hero formula.
Lighting/mood: luminous bone surfaces against deep ink, subtle film grain and edge halation, confident, precise, cinematic, expensive.
Color palette: near-black ink, luminous bone, muted silver, and one restrained signal red only.
Materials/textures: uncoated paper fiber, matte black substrate, faint registration ink marks without letters, brushed screen-glass reflections, print grain, newsprint texture.
Text: none. Do not render any visible text, letters, words, numbers, labels, captions, titles, taglines, axis values, tick numbers, pseudo-text, glyphs, logos, signatures, or watermarks anywhere in the image.
Text-safe construction: browser headers must be empty black bars with only simple red square indicators; market evidence rows must be blank lines and solid blocks only; graph axes must be completely unlabeled; crop marks and grid measurements must use line segments and ticks only; no alphanumeric symbols may appear in textures or portal imagery.
Constraints: one landscape cover, five visually distinct portal frames, generous quiet left third, clear hierarchy, refined spacing, professional fictional documentation artwork, no third-party identity.
Avoid: all typography and typographic marks, pseudo-writing, fake UI copy, chart labels, axis artifacts, numbers, emblems, logos, watermarks, glossy gradient SaaS art, purple-blue AI glow, floating 3D blobs, generic dashboard cards, fake awards, copied website identities, meaningless icons, rounded pill overload, stock-template brand boards.

title: MORPH-17
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: fictional regenerative-biology research platform desktop interface for documentation
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity wide desktop interface for MORPH-17, a fictional regenerative-biology research platform. The screen must feel like a credible contemporary laboratory instrument translated to the web, not science fiction.
Scene/backdrop: Sterile white lab-film canvas with a large off-center radial microscopy specimen viewport showing plausible fluorescent cell morphology, ringed by precise assay bands and optical calibration marks. Build asymmetric diagnostic panels around it, an uninterrupted vertical assay timeline along the far right, and a slim data legend integrated into the outer edge rather than floating in a card.
Style/medium: clinical interface art direction, optical microscopy photography, advanced information design, crisp neo-grotesk typography, restrained scientific visualization, implementation-clear desktop UI.
Composition/framing: 16:9 landscape. The microscopy circle dominates the left-center and deliberately breaks the grid; thin diagnostic strips bridge to the right. A translucent film layer crosses only one quadrant. Sharp hairline separators and measured whitespace. Responsive cue: a compact lower diagnostic strip visually demonstrates how the edge legend and assay timeline can reflow beneath the specimen on a narrow screen.
Lighting/mood: cool transmitted-light microscopy, sterile daylight, translucent refractive depth, calm precision, credible and analytical.
Color palette: sterile white and very pale cool gray, deep indigo as the anchor, cytoplasm green inside scientific imagery, ultraviolet used only as a tiny analytical accent.
Materials/textures: translucent laboratory film, etched glass, microscopy grain, polished optical coating, paper-thin hairlines.
Typography: clinical neo-grotesk for interface structure and clean tabular monospace for sparse measurement values. High legibility and restrained scale.
Text (verbatim): "MORPH-17". Render this name exactly and correctly as the only readable phrase. Numeric ticks and measurement values may appear only if clean and sparse; no other words, abbreviations, fake paragraphs, or pseudo-language.
Constraints: data must appear structured and biologically plausible; no claim of real data; no company logo or emblem; all-sharp system; distinct radial composition; one obvious assay-sequence interaction; fictional documentation artwork.
Interaction implication: concentric assay bands imply rotating specimen focus; the right timeline implies vertical sample progression; one selected interval aligns across the viewport and diagnostic strips.
Avoid: neon cyberpunk, dark hacker UI, generic SaaS cards, crypto aesthetics, impossible anatomical imagery, DNA-helix clichés, excessive glow, glossy gradient backgrounds, dashboard card spam, logos, watermarks, copied lab-software identities, illegible microcopy, malformed cells, random decorative particles.

title: COMMON LEDGER
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: fictional public-market intelligence terminal desktop interface for documentation
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity wide desktop public-market intelligence terminal titled COMMON LEDGER. It must fuse radical financial brutalism with print-led research, clearly unlike a conventional dark fintech dashboard.
Scene/backdrop: Dense newsprint-white modular ledger covered by hard tar-black rules. A split ticker band cuts across both the top edge and a lower third. One enormous stencil numeric anchor, "4.27", occupies a structural quadrant. A very narrow thesis column is squeezed against the left rail while expandable evidence rows form a severe horizontal stack on the right.
Style/medium: brutalist editorial information design, industrial newspaper terminal, thermal-printer artifacts, stamped annotation marks, machine labels, implementation-clear desktop UI.
Composition/framing: 16:9 landscape. Strict sharp-corner grid with intentionally unequal modules: compressed thesis rail, oversized central numeric field, deep evidence-row region, and two ticker bands moving in opposing directions. A snap-to-period navigator is integrated as a heavy segmented ruler crossing the numeric field. Responsive cue: a narrow inset strip near the bottom shows the ledger reorganized into one vertical sequence with sticky ticker and expandable rows.
Lighting/mood: flat print-table illumination, severe, urgent, rigorous, public-record atmosphere. No glossy depth.
Color palette: aged newsprint white and tar black dominate; safety orange for stamped decisions; electric blue for one active period and one evidence link. No gradients.
Materials/textures: coarse newsprint fiber, thermal-print grain, rubber-stamp ink, slightly misregistered overprint, metal stencil impressions.
Typography: condensed industrial sans for major labels, tabular monospace for values, stencil numerals for the oversized anchor. Dense but with unmistakable hierarchy.
Text (verbatim): "COMMON LEDGER" and "4.27". Render both exactly and correctly. Other visible content may be clean numeric values, ticker-like abbreviations of no more than four letters, and simple symbols only; never render paragraphs or pseudo-language.
Interaction implication: the heavy period ruler visibly snaps between segments; evidence rows expose alternating collapsed and expanded states using structural height, not rounded cards.
Constraints: fictional documentation artwork, plausible public-market research structure, high information density, sharp rectangular system, no company logos, no real market brand identity, no claim of live data.
Avoid: Bloomberg imitation, Stripe or Linear visual language, crypto exchanges, generic dark dashboards, glossy finance cards, rounded SaaS panels, gradients, neon glow, logos, watermarks, fake stock-brand names, illegible microtext, chart clutter without hierarchy, three identical stat cards.
